prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Create a pitch-quality photoreal 3D packaging and branding concept for "Hungry 4 Munchies", a burger fast-food-inspired collectible brick construction set.
REFERENCE INPUT ROLES: the user's two restaurant photos supply only mood: warm mustard/red retro LA fast-food interior, streetwear energy, candid flash attitude. The tiny burger logo supplies brand inspiration, interpret it into a polished original burger-shaped badge and bold wordmark. The last image is the EXACT BRICK BURGER PRODUCT: preserve its tan curved LEGO-style bun with six white sesame tiles, red tomato, lime/green ruffled lettuce, square yellow cheese, brown patty, tan bottom bun, brick seams and proportions. Do not turn it into food or invent a different model. No people needed.
CONCEPT 01 — CLASSIC DRIVE-THRU. One beautifully art-directed landscape 3:2 full 3D product hero image, not a moodboard, not a flat box dieline. A large closed premium folding carton at rear-left viewed from a three-quarter angle showing full front, right side and top; a matching open burger clamshell presentation carton rear-right with custom cream tissue and a structured product cavity; and the actual assembled 4.4-inch-wide brick burger prominently in the front. Packaging sized plausibly for the product, roughly 7-inch square footprint. Every box fully visible, grounded, no cropping.
Design a complete cohesive brand system with bold rounded 1970s diner letterforms and an original stylized burger badge. Ketchup red, warm mustard yellow, vanilla cream, dark chocolate, subtle green accent. Oversized wraparound stripes, playful checker strip, expressive sticker-like type and tiny brick-stud motifs. Premium screen-printed cardboard, believable fold lines, matte paper and subtle spot gloss. Brand wordmark largest on front: "Hungry 4 Munchies". Display exact tagline "FLAVURR!" prominently on lid/top in huge type. Exact tagline "GaahhhDayumm!" on open inner lid. Secondary clear product name "BRICK BURGER" and small "767 PIECES" and "6 STACKABLE LAYERS". A printed illustration of the actual brick burger on the box, not a meat photograph. Set on a cream diner counter with restrained red/mustard horizon bands, tasteful hard flash plus soft studio fill, crisp dimensional shadows, realistic premium commercial CGI. Make this feel like a coveted fast-food collaboration toy drop. Strong composition and readable type. No LEGO logo, no Pioneer Chicken or Pepsi logos, no made-up endorsements, no extraneous filler copy. Exact spelling for both catchphrases.

Use case: product-mockup. Generate the SECOND DISTINCT 3D packaging concept for the Hungry 4 Munchies BRICK BURGER pitch. This must be a new art direction, not a recolor of the previous cream/red carton.
INPUT ROLES: user restaurant photos = fast-food streetwear mood only, no people; user tiny burger-logo = brand reference; original clean tan brick-burger render = actual product geometry reference; previous generated classic packaging image = brand family and product consistency only, change packaging design and silhouette.
CONCEPT 02 — LATE-NIGHT FLAVURR. A premium collectible toy drop meets a loud after-dark burger joint. Deep near-black chocolate cardboard with oversized electric red/orange "FLAVURR!" custom lettering, acid mustard yellow flashes, bright cream type, small cobalt blue accent stickers. Chunky original burger badge reading exactly "Hungry 4 Munchies", green HUNGRY, yellow 4, red MUNCHIES, cream outline; prominently integrated in the design. Side-panel exact "GaahhhDayumm!" in wild bold outlined script. Strong typography, oversized cropped graphic lettering ON the panels but brand name fully legible. Black/cream racing checks, tiny stud icons, rhythmic retro halftone illustration. Graphics printed with convincing spot UV and raised logo, not neon glowing signage.
ONE full photoreal 3D landscape 3:2 commercial product shot: a CLOSED rigid squat rectangular collector box with a sliding sleeve to left/back, three visible faces and complete silhouette; a matching inner drawer partially pulled out to the right showing branded paper and a product cavity; the actual assembled brick hamburger out front on its printed fast-food tray liner. Every item entirely in frame with generous edge margin. Product must be immediately identifiable as the original brick construction hamburger, not edible food: preserve tan curved bun with six white tile sesame pieces, red tomato, lime/green lettuce, square yellow cheese, brown patty, tan bottom bun, visible tile/plate seams. Plausible scale: burger 4.4 inches across, package about 7 inches across. On sleeve a large clean image of that brick burger and smaller diagram of six separated ingredients. Print exact "BRICK BURGER", "767 PIECES", "6 STACKABLE LAYERS". Place exact "FLAVURR!" on the box top in huge type and exact "GaahhhDayumm!" on the drawer inside panel. Cinematic warm direct-flash product photography on a brushed stainless diner counter, dark red vinyl booth softly out of focus, controlled specular highlights, professional studio CGI, tactile luxurious printed cardboard. Strong clean visual hierarchy. No people, no LEGO logo, no Pepsi or Pioneer Chicken branding, no unrelated logos, no watermark, no invented partnership text. This is an original packaging pitch.

Use case: product-mockup. Create a THIRD genuinely distinct full 3D packaging design for Hungry 4 Munchies' collectible BRICK BURGER. This is a pitch concept for a brick construction model, not edible food.
REFERENCE ROLES: restaurant photograph is atmosphere only; tiny original burger-logo reference is the brand cue; clean original brick burger render is the product to preserve closely; prior two generated images establish identity but their box structures, layouts and graphics should NOT be repeated.
CONCEPT 03 — RETRO TAKEOUT CLUB. Forest green + warm ivory + mustard gold, with precise tomato-red accent. Original confident stacked rounded slab-serif wordmark "Hungry 4 Munchies", styled as a vintage burger stand logo, an oversized 4 and a small sesame-bun arch. Smart editorial restraint but still joyful fast food. Diagonal green/ivory barber stripes, sesame-dot pattern and a bold oval quality-style badge with only the real brand wording. Use exact catchphrases "FLAVURR!" and "GaahhhDayumm!". Clean beautiful typography, meticulously printed physical packaging, paper grain and folds.
SCENE: single landscape 3:2 professional photoreal three-quarter product rendering on a warm ivory tabletop. The packaging MUST be a wide LOW square hinged burger clamshell collector carton, approximately 7 x 7 x 4 inches — not an upright toy box. One CLOSED low carton at rear-left, lid printed with the giant brand wordmark and a small graphic illustration of the brick burger; a matching OPEN low carton rear-right, lifted hinged lid saying "GaahhhDayumm!" in tomato-red script, an ivory sculpted pulp insert containing the brick hamburger. At front, a SECOND sample of the actual brick hamburger standing out of the box, entirely visible. A partially slipped green belly band around the closed carton reads "FLAVURR!" in gigantic ivory rounded italic letters. Minimal cream instruction booklet next to the burger with the brand mark and "BRICK BURGER". On carton front lip exact "767 PIECES" and "6 STACKABLE LAYERS". All objects fully in frame, generous breathing room. Box perspective and construction physically convincing.
PRODUCT: retain the original tan layered bun and curved slopes, six white sesame tiles, red tomato band, lime and green ruffled lettuce, square yellow cheese, brown patty, tan lower bun, recognizable brick seams. Product is about 4.4 inches across and 2.77 inches high. No edible burger, no organic food texture.
LIGHTING: warm soft editorial studio daylight with crisp pleasant shadows, high-quality ray-traced look, subtle green shadow accents, no busy restaurant background. Art direction like a beautifully crafted independent LA burger brand meets a collectible design object. Show the printed front, side and top panels of the full boxes, with premium realistic cardboard materials. No other company logos, no LEGO logo, no Pepsi or Pioneer logos, no people, no fake endorsement, no made-up extra taglines, no watermark. Exact text spelling must be legible.
